subject: Lake Kivu
title: A Lake in Africa Could Explode. Two Million People Live Around It

scenes.text: There's a lake in Africa that could explode. Two million people live around it.
Lake Kivu looks calm. But its deep water holds about three hundred cubic kilometres of gas.
Carbon dioxide and methane, locked down by the weight of the water above.
Like the cap on a soda bottle.
If the deep water ever rolled over, it could release a suffocating cloud. A smaller lake in Cameroon did that in 1986.
So Rwanda is pumping the gas up and burning it for electricity.

description:
Lake Kivu, on the border of Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, holds roughly 300 cubic kilometres of dissolved carbon dioxide and methane in its deep layers, and about two million people live around it.
In 1986 a similar gas release from Lake Nyos in Cameroon killed more than 1,700 people. At Kivu, power plants now extract the methane to generate electricity, which also slowly lowers the risk.
Would you live next to a lake like this?
first_comment: The gas has built up over centuries. Would you trust a power plant to keep it in check, or move away?
